To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) fibroblast-derived MT- MMP promotes tumor progression in HNSCC in vitro and in mouse models, 2) MT- MMP null fibroblast co-injection reduces tumor growth by >90%, and 3) MMP-2 null or MMP-9 null co-injection reduces growth by ~50%.
fibroblast derived MT1-MMP, but not MMP-2, promotes tumor progression in HNSCC.
fibroblast-derived MT-MMP is required for HNSCC tumor cell invasion in vitro and growth in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of fibroblast-derived factors in tumor progression and the development of novel molecular therapies that target these factors.
the role of the tumor microenvironment in tumor progression and metastasis.
identifying fibroblast derived MMPs and other factors involved in tumor cell growth and invasion in HNSCC.

MT1-MMP derived from fibroblasts plays an important role in tumor progression.
MT1-MMP is a critical factor for HNSCC invasion and tumor growth in the context of fibroblast-tumor cell interaction.
MT1-MMP derived from fibroblasts promotes tumor cell invasion and growth in vitro and in a floor of mouth mouse xenograft model.
